threads.body: [General] Deferred body chunks received through `onResponseContent` or `onResponseContentAsync` can lose the captured caller context, making application spans roots instead of siblings of the CLIENT span. In Jetty 12.0.0, invoking `AsyncContentListener.onContentSource()` on the original listener registers demand callbacks that bypass this proxy after its scope closes. Wrap content-source demand callbacks with the captured context and add coverage where body data arrives after the initial notification.

@copilot Update this PR directly to fix the production pending-demand failure-path issue identified in the body of Copilot review 5640450773: https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/pull/20934#pullrequestreview-5640450773. The user explicitly approved extending the preceding test-only work to fix this production issue in cloud. Do not create another PR.

The failure premise is verified against the supported org.eclipse.jetty:jetty-client:12.0.0 source. ResponseListeners.notifyContentSource(Response, Content.Source) hands the source to ContentSourceDemultiplexer when multiple content listeners exist. That demultiplexer creates separate Content.Source instances for its listeners. Its per-listener source stores the listener's demand callback, and fail(Throwable) directly invokes onDemandCallback() on the failing thread before registerFailure(). The existing javaagent advice wraps only the source passed to the public notifyContentSource method. The per-listener demand callbacks therefore remain unwrapped on this failure path and lose the captured caller context when failed from another thread.

Fix this at the per-listener source handoff in instrumentation/jetty-httpclient/jetty-httpclient-12.0/javaagent/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/javaagent/instrumentation/jetty/httpclient/v12_0/JettyClient12ResponseListenersInstrumentation.java. Jetty 12.0.0 has a private static notifyContentSource(Response.ContentSourceListener, Response, Content.Source) helper that also dispatches the demultiplexer-created sources. Target that dispatch for content-source wrapping and adjust the advice's response/source argument bindings and argument replacement consistently. Verify the concrete signatures and dispatch paths across the supported Jetty versions before choosing the matcher. Preserve existing public notification scoping; do not move response callbacks under the CLIENT span.

Add focused regression coverage through the installed javaagent and real supported Jetty listener lifecycle: register multiple response-content listeners, establish pending demand on a per-listener source, then fail it from another thread carrying an unrelated Context. Verify the demand callback observes the full captured caller Context, including span parentage and a custom Context value, and that the failing thread's original context is restored afterward. Preserve library behavior and reuse shared coverage when it exercises the same supported lifecycle without unnecessary duplicate tests. Ensure the test deterministically exercises the per-listener failure path rather than just ordinary chunk delivery; use bounded synchronization, not fixed sleeps.

Keep the completed simplifications and other request/response behavior intact. Preserve backpressure, chunk ownership/release, failure/completion semantics, callers without spans, and support from Jetty 12.0.0 onward. Make the smallest complete fix for this failure path, run narrow relevant formatting and library/javaagent tests with baseline/latest dependencies when available, and report actual validation or JDK blockers. The supported Jetty 12.0.0 HttpRequest.body(Content) simply replaces the field; HttpSender calls request.notifyBegin() before ContentSender reads request.getBody(). Therefore AsyncRequestContent.write(..., Callback) application completion can escape the caller scope, including under the enclosing library CLIENT scope or an unrelated completion thread. @copilot Update this existing PR directly to fix the substantive body-only finding in review 5641811059: https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/pull/20934#pullrequestreview-5641811059. Despite its 'No open issues' badge, the review describes a real combined library/javaagent callback-context defect. The previous coding attempt is finished and its delegation thread is resolved. No new PR or unrelated audit work.

With an installed javaagent and a real client created by JettyClientTelemetry.createHttpClient(), TracingHttpRequest.send captures the caller, starts the library CLIENT span, and makes that CLIENT context current around super.send. Agent advice on the base HttpRequest.send then unconditionally overwrites JETTY_CLIENT_CONTEXT_KEY with this CLIENT context before checking whether its own instrumenter starts anything. Later the library notifyBegin/notifyQueued/etc overrides enter the true caller scope, but their calls to super.notify* hit agent notify advice which reinstalls the stored CLIENT context immediately around the actual application request hook. Nested application spans therefore become children of CLIENT instead of the caller, even when duplicate agent span creation is suppressed.

Prevent redundant agent callback scoping from overriding library-owned caller boundaries, or otherwise preserve the actual library-captured caller through this supported combined path. Trace ownership and suppression before choosing the smallest reliable solution. Do not assume a library Context object can be cast to the agent's shaded Context across isolation boundaries, use brittle unrestricted class-name exclusions, remove justified internal CLIENT execution, or weaken plain-agent caller propagation just because a span was suppressed. Preserve normal library-only and agent-only behavior, custom Context values and baggage, callers without a span, and restoration of unrelated callback-thread state.

Add a regression using the installed agent with the public JettyClientTelemetry API creating the actual instrumented client. Exercise a request hook such as onRequestBegin that starts an application span and an independently instrumented nested HTTP request, and verify caller parentage, no duplicate CLIENT operation, full caller Context including a no-parent case, remote propagation, and completion/restoration. Check the late-body/trailer/chunk callback boundaries remain correct in this combined setup rather than merely unit-testing a helper or mocking suppression.

Keep all delivered response-consumption, deferred content-demand/failure, late body replacement, trailer supplier, asynchronous chunk-release callback, span-lifetime, and outgoing propagation fixes. The preceding attempt explicitly left its final installed-agent rerun after non-inlined AssignReturned argument replacement unverified. Run focused actual-current-head installed-agent coverage of the new body/trailer setters and this combined case, plus relevant library coverage and narrow formatting when feasible; report exact outcomes or concrete environment blockers, not an unqualified pass. Preserve the current public API and configuration. #20958 stays open for the full audit. Acceptance is correct application caller context under library-only, agent-only, and combined instrumentation without losing transport, lifecycle, or suppression behavior.

[General] `Context.wrap(callback)` drops Jetty's `Invocable` invocation type, so nonblocking demand callbacks are classified as blocking. In supported Jetty 12.1, this changes response-read scheduling and can add unnecessary executor handoffs, including for the agent's default content-consumption path. Preserve the original invocation type around the context-wrapped callback with `Invocable.from(...)`.
